name: Night Light
tagline: You were small too. You looked after them anyway.
epigraph: Part of the taste in this glass comes from something that stayed behind in the barrel.
glassware: a small stemmed cocktail glass, chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. Line that lands: "You were never less scared of the dark. You just had someone to be calm for." 4-grams checked against every pour and clean ("the people you love", lover-regular-guy, and "someone close to you", the Nurse, both moved off). No brother, sister, sibling or eldest; "someone littler" covers a cousin, a friend or a parent. The chamomile is an ode to the watch, never said to calm anyone. "First" kept out of the title block (the Angel's "The basil gets there first"). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/flor.md` (F1–F16): *Cocktail Codex* pp. 245–247; Consejo Regulador, sherry.wine "Ageing" (secondary, the DO's own body); Luyten, *SherryNotes* 2013 (secondary); Valcárcel-Muñoz et al., *Molecules* 27(2):365 (2022), doi 10.3390/molecules27020365 (peer-reviewed, the almond); *Oxford Companion* BRANDY DE JEREZ pdf 346. Drink: *Cocktail Codex* pp. 72, 75, 77, 83, 91, 92, 188, 280; David Wondrich, *Imbibe!* pdf 210 (the Bamboo, "a fino or an amontillado"; Boothby's French-vermouth version); *Flavor Matrix* Grape pdf 140 (honey). Set aside: rye (Oxford RYE pdf 1714–1715: the Underdog's shape) and the Robertson sisters (motive contested). Room notes: `work/innocent-caregiver/`.
names_note: **Night Light**, the room's pick (all three, rounds 5–7): what the person was for someone smaller, the small light left on so the dark isn't total. It makes sense cold, names the person rather than the yeast, and keeps "first" out of the title block. Also considered: *Stayed Up*, *Quiet Company* (Tomás; rhymes with the closing line), *The Air Reaches You First* (Wren's working title; "first" beside the Angel's epigraph, and y2 already says it). Set aside by Tomás: *Smaller by Morning* ("by morning" is in *Four Shares*), *Still Awake* (beside *Still Yours*), *Under the Veil* (reads as concealment).
open_items: **Two cellar organisms in one family (for Robin).** The Free Spirit's plan lead is the black fungus on warehouse walls; this pour is the flor. Owned in words (no walls, cellar, evaporation, "feeds on", "lives on", fungus, mould, black; "dark" only as the child's fear) and in the image briefs (their black walls, our ivory veil). Flagged by Wren and Hester.

**The family plan was overturned.** The plan's lead was rye (Oxford RYE); Wren struck it in round 1 as the Underdog's scorned-then-useful shape, protecting nobody smaller. Petraske stays the Lover family's. The room chose flor in round 3; the plan row carries the note.

**Clause 4 of Wren's story test** reads "a cost or effort". The flor's only cost on any page is its end (amontillado), which the test rules out; the room ruled on effort: the flor keeps the air off and breathes up most of the oxygen itself (sherry.wine; Luyten "most of"). Fino only: amontillado and palo cortado stay out.

**Strength and acid read OUT on Arnold's stirred ranges** because the core is wine (11.7% / 4.25 g sugar / 0.38% acid). Tomás justifies it, not fixes it: a spirit core is what *Codex* p. 246 says drowns a fino; the *Codex*'s own Bamboo runs 13.4% / 3.07 g / 0.41% on the same formula. Sugar is in range.

**Chamomile** is in the daisy family; the allergy is named in Checks, and no veto covers it. The chamomile-honey syrup row was first made for the Angel's retired *The Rest of You*; no live pour has it. Plain honey syrup is a fallback that changes no number.

**Makeable:** an opened fino should be corked, kept in the fridge and used within a week or so (*Codex* p. 246). Kept out of the closing line on purpose (it would hand the guest another watch to keep).
**The Bamboo's origin is contested** three ways (Boothby credits Eppinger; Wondrich hedges; the *Codex* says Japan). The reading gives none, only "on record by 1886".
